From: Data Protection <dpo@legacyops.com>

Date: 2026-12-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: temporary addition of on-prem analytics processor (EdgeLogix)

Hi Olga,

Hope you’re well. We’re preparing a short-term integration with a local analytics processor (EdgeLogix) to accelerate log ingestion for a pilot in our EMEA clusters. The plan is temporary (6-8 weeks) and scope-limited to telemetry aggregation; no customer PII is intended to be shared, but the processor will see hashed session IDs and request metadata.

We need the following from Redwood to proceed:
- Confirmation you can add EdgeLogix to the subprocessor roster for LegacyOps (EU tenancy)
- A DPA addendum or temporary subprocessor annex we can sign
- Export/data-flow map that shows whether any telemetry could transit outside the EU

Attaching the processor roster and a short technical note on the integration. Please let us know if you need more details.

Thanks,
Marta Kovacs
Data Protection Lead | LegacyOps

Kimberly / Rishi,

Forwarding LegacyOps' ask — short pilot, EU-only tenancy per their note, wants EdgeLogix added as subprocessor for ~6–8 weeks. I pulled the roster they attached. Initial thoughts: we need a quick but defensible decision rationale.

Can you please review and respond with recommended position by EOD?
- Kimberly: can we produce a one-off DPA addendum that limits processing scope and includes an onshore-only commitment?
- Rishi: please run a data-flow check — any export risk? Also flag operational mitigations (encryption, tokenization) we must require if we proceed.

If we decline, we should provide an alternative (e.g., a sandboxed telemetry adapter or our hosted telemetry proxy) and rationale that we can share with the customer.

Olga / Rishi,

I had a quick look at the roster and Edgelogix's public docs. Summary: they do not present EEA residency certifications and their connectivity model includes optional downstream replication to a US-based analytics cluster by default. That creates a non-trivial export risk unless EdgeLogix can confirm configuration to fully disable outbound replication.

Compliance perspective: adding them as a subprocessor for EU tenancy without explicit export safeguards or an approved onshore-only commitment is a material change to our DPA. Our options are:
1) Decline the addition and propose Redwood-hosted telemetry proxy + limited-scope CSV export (preferred)
2) Approve conditionally if LegacyOps obtains a signed annex with EdgeLogix promising no cross-border replication, certificate of EEA processing, and KMS-enforced keys with customer-controlled rotations

I drafted suggested language for a DPA addendum (see attached) and redlines to our standard subprocessor annex. If we decline, I recommend we use the following wording to the customer: a compliance-driven decline citing exportability and lack of onshore guarantees, plus an offer of an alternative technical route. Keep it firm but solution-oriented.

Attachments: initial-assessment-notes.txt (notes), redlined-dpa-suggestion.pdf (redline)

Kimberly
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Marta Kovacs <dpo@legacyops.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-16T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary addition of on-prem analytics processor (EdgeLogix) — Decline & next steps

Marta,

Thanks for the details and the roster you sent. After an internal compliance and technical review we cannot approve EdgeLogix as a temporary subprocessor for your EU tenancy under the current controls. The primary concerns are:
- Edgelogix’s default replication options include non-EEA endpoints and the vendor did not provide a certificate or audit evidence of EEA-only processing.
- Without KMS controls scoped to the EU tenancy and documented onshore-only configuration, adding them could trigger cross-border transfer obligations we cannot accept for this tenancy.

That said, we want to keep the pilot moving. Two practical next steps we propose:
1) If EdgeLogix can provide a signed annex (sample language attached) that commits to onshore-only processing for the EEA tenancy, KMS configuration notes, and an attestation of no US replication within the pilot window, Redwood will re-open review immediately. Please note we will require evidence (logs/config) proving the configuration before going live.
2) As an alternative we can deploy Redwood’s hosted telemetry proxy (limited-scope adapter) for the pilot. This avoids adding a third-party subprocessor and preserves EU residency while providing the performance characteristics you need. We can scope a short-term pricing overlay for the pilot.

I’ve attached a template DPA addendum that outlines the minimal controls we’d require. Let us know which path you prefer and, if you pursue the annex with EdgeLogix, share the signed document and configuration evidence.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Privacy Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: dpa_addendum_template.docx (document)
